On 12 April 2019 the Security Council adopted the United States draft S/2019/311 as resolution 2466 by 13 votes to none, with the Dominican Republic and Russia abstaining. Acting under Chapter VII, it extended MINUJUSTH for a final six months until 15 October. It requested the Secretary-General to plan a successor United Nations presence including a special political mission.

France argued that Chapter VII language empowers MINUJUSTH to complete its mandate and implement the Secretary-General's recommendations. Russia objected, stating that applying Chapter VII to the entire mandate, including human rights monitoring, is inappropriate as it does not constitute a threat to international peace. The Council decided to adopt the resolution with Chapter VII language limited strictly to security and stabilization components, excluding human rights monitoring from enforcement measures.
